questions.question: When stopping a manual transmission vehicle, what should you do?

options.text: Push the clutch in when the engine is almost at idle speed.
Push the clutch out when the engine is almost at idle speed.
Shift into neutral when the engine is almost at idle speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Push the clutch in when the engine is almost at idle speed.
questions.explanation: When stopping, apply steady pressure to the brake pedal and stop smoothly. For a manual transmission vehicle, push the clutch in when the engine is almost at idle speed.

questions.question: What should you do before entering a curve?
questions.correctAnswerText: Shift to a lower gear.
questions.explanation: Always shift to a lower gear before entering a curve. Slowing down before the curve helps you keep better control of your vehicle while turning.

questions.question: What happens if ABS is only on one axle?

options.text: You still have better control when braking.
It slows the vehicle but cannot stop it.

questions.correctAnswerText: You still have better control when braking.
questions.explanation: Even if ABS is only on one axle, you still have more braking control than a vehicle without ABS. Brake normally.

questions.question: If a traffic light has been green for a long time, what will likely happen?

options.text: It will probably stay green as you approach.
It will likely turn yellow soon.
It will skip yellow and go straight to red.

questions.correctAnswerText: It will likely turn yellow soon.
questions.explanation: If a traffic light has been green for a long time, it will probably turn yellow before you reach it. Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: What happens when a combination vehicle turns a corner?

options.text: The vehicle must use at least two lanes.
The front and rear wheels follow different paths.
It is best to let the rear wheels drive over the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: The front and rear wheels follow different paths.
questions.explanation: When a vehicle turns a corner, the rear wheels follow a different path than the front wheels. This is called off-tracking. It is more noticeable on vehicles with trailers.

questions.question: When starting a vehicle, what should warning lights and buzzers do?

options.text: Should not light up or sound.
Should turn on and turn off quickly.
Should turn on and stay on.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should turn on and turn off quickly.
questions.explanation: After you start the engine, warning lights and buzzers should turn on and then quickly turn off.

questions.question: When should you check and adjust your mirrors?
questions.correctAnswerText: Before driving.
questions.explanation: Always check your mirrors before you start driving. Your posture changes day to day, so your mirrors may need adjustment.

questions.question: An air supply control lever should be in its normal position when you are:
questions.correctAnswerText: Pulling a trailer.
questions.explanation: Older vehicles may have levers instead of knobs for tractor protection controls. When an air supply control is in its normal position, it is set correctly for pulling a trailer.

questions.question: What happens if air pressure is lost in the emergency line?

options.text: The tractor protection valve will open.
The trailer will detach from the tractor.

questions.correctAnswerText: The emergency brakes will activate.
questions.explanation: The emergency air line controls the emergency brakes. If air pressure is lost in the emergency line, the emergency trailer brakes will activate.

questions.question: When you press the brake pedal, how quickly do air brakes work?

options.text: Only if it is warm outside.

questions.correctAnswerText: After a short delay.
questions.explanation: Air takes time to travel through the air lines to reach the brakes. There is a brake lag of at least half a second between when you press the pedal and when the brakes start to work.

questions.question: When you start a vehicle, the oil pressure should:

options.text: Slowly build up over a few minutes.
Reach normal level within a few seconds.
Start high, then drop quickly while the engine runs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reach normal level within a few seconds.
questions.explanation: After you start the engine, oil pressure should reach normal level within seconds. Do not drive if the oil pressure is low, dropping, or unstable.

questions.question: After changing a tire, you should stop after driving a short distance to:

options.text: Check that the lug nuts are tight.
Look for rocks in the tire tread.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check that the lug nuts are tight.
questions.explanation: After you start driving with a new tire, stop after a short distance to make sure the lug nuts are still tight.

questions.question: When driving downhill, your vehicle will:

options.text: Move at the same speed as on flat ground.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up.
questions.explanation: Gravity makes your vehicle go faster downhill. Slow down before you reach a downgrade.

questions.question: To prevent fatigue on long trips, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Take frequent breaks.
questions.explanation: To avoid fatigue on a long trip, take a break every 100 miles or every two hours. Driving at night or when you would normally sleep increases fatigue risk.

questions.question: When braking on a downgrade, slow down until you reach a speed that is:
questions.correctAnswerText: 5 mph below your safe speed.
questions.explanation: When driving downhill, brake until your vehicle reaches 5 mph below your safe speed. Then release the brake and repeat this process.

questions.question: To exit your parking space as safely as possible, you should park:

options.text: So that you must back up to leave.
So that you can drive forward to leave.
On the side of a road, not in a parking lot.

questions.correctAnswerText: So that you can drive forward to leave.
questions.explanation: Backing is dangerous. Park so you can drive forward to exit your space when possible.

questions.question: When driving down a steep hill:

options.text: Shift to a lower gear, then use brakes to add to the engine's braking power.
Downshift instead of using the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift to a lower gear, then use brakes to add to the engine's braking power.
questions.explanation: The engine's braking power should be your main way to control speed on a downgrade. Shift to a lower gear before going down the hill. Use brakes only for extra slowing or stopping if needed.

questions.question: During a pre-trip inspection, after starting the engine you should:

options.text: Put the engine in first gear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Listen for unusual noises.
questions.explanation: Check your engine during the pre-trip inspection. After starting it, listen for any strange sounds.

questions.question: When driving on a wet road, reduce your speed by:
questions.correctAnswerText: About one-third.
questions.explanation: Reduce your speed on wet roads that have less grip. Slow down by about one-third on wet roads.

questions.question: In very hot weather, check your tires regularly because:

options.text: Air pressure may increase with the heat.
The tread wears faster in hot weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Air pressure may increase with the heat.
questions.explanation: Air pressure rises when temperatures are hot. Check your tire pressure and mounting carefully when driving in hot weather.
